answer: One defence is IPFS content routing proof: a file the node can serve to strangers, and the meadow of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. Verification takes a second and costs almost nothing, while a file the node can serve to strangers takes days to arrange for each new name; the pearl is a gap the farm cannot close by spending more on servers. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the marble of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
